Rebecca's fears, whatever they were, were not rational, and Christine, who initially did not want to go, ultimately stayed, when she could have asked for help for herself, for her nephew, for Rebecca. 

I'm not placing any blame. I don't think either of these women wanted this to happen, even if they preferred it to an imaginary future. At some point they became in capable of making a rational assessment of the danger they were in, and they had successfully isolated themselves to the point that no-one could intervene on their behalf. It's a genuine tragedy. 

Mother Nature may be harsh, leaves no quarter, takes no prisoners -- mental illness does. comments.text: A lifestraw in itself is perfectly fine for a main filter in the outdoors (more for hiking... cause weight)... buuuut, as with any gear in the outdoors (or just being there), especially long term, it's all about risk management and having backup plans. A lifestraw is a purely mechanical filter that filters out particulates of a certain size and above. It will filter out pretty much all bacteria and parasites, but not viruses and obviously not organic and inorganic toxins. Viruses tend to be highly species specific, so it isn't that much of a deal to not filter them out, and if the water source is reasonable, then it most likely also doesn't contain any other toxins. You're still taking a risk of course. Boiling the water in addition, or using water purification tablets can increase the safety... but for such a long term stay, it would make much more sense to use a proper multistage filter setup that which will remove pretty much anything. Anyway, a proper gps emergency beacon is imho a must for such adventures, even when experienced, cause if something happens, like you falling into a pit and breaking your ankle, it quickly goes from perfectly fine to a life and death struggle.
